definition: To change to suit a new situation.
example: We adapt our plans when the weather changes.

definition: Something that makes a situation better or easier.
example: A small class has the advantage of more speaking time.

definition: A situation in which different parts receive suitable attention.
example: I try to keep a balance between study and rest.

definition: A task or situation that tests your ability.
example: Reading my first novel was a challenge.

definition: People connected by a place or a shared interest.
example: Our community meets to clean the park.

definition: Feeling sure about your ability or an outcome.
example: I feel confident when I practise before a presentation.

definition: A result caused by an action or event.
example: Missing the bus was a consequence of leaving late.

definition: Able to produce new and interesting ideas.
example: Our group found a creative solution.

definition: Working well without wasting time or effort.
example: The new bus route is more efficient.

definition: To give someone support or confidence.
example: We encourage each other to speak English.

definition: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives.
example: Plants need a suitable environment to grow.

definition: Knowledge gained from doing or seeing things.
example: She has experience of working with children.

definition: Able or willing to change when needed.
example: A flexible timetable helps busy learners.

definition: Willing to give time, help, or money.
example: Our generous neighbour shares vegetables from her garden.

definition: Able to act without needing others to help.
example: The project helps students become independent learners.

definition: A situation that allows you to do something.
example: The trip is an opportunity to practise English.

definition: Able to wait calmly or keep trying.
example: Be patient while your partner finds the right word.

definition: Able to be trusted to work well or do what is expected.
example: We need a reliable bus service.

definition: A way of dealing with a problem.
example: Drawing a map was a simple solution.

definition: Someone who offers to help without being paid.
example: A volunteer reads stories at the library.

definition: Having more than one possible meaning.
example: The ambiguous instruction confused the group.
synonyms: open to more than one reading

definition: To examine something carefully to understand it.
example: We analyse the results before making a decision.

definition: To expect something and prepare for it.
example: We anticipate a busy afternoon, so we have extra staff ready.

definition: Something accepted as true without enough proof.
example: Our plan relied on the assumption that everyone had a phone.

definition: To work with others on a shared task.
example: The two classes collaborate on a school newspaper.

definition: An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wants.
example: We reached a compromise about the meeting time.

definition: Acting or happening in a similar way over time.
example: Consistent practice helps new words stay in your memory.

definition: To give something as part of a shared effort.
example: Everyone can contribute an idea to the discussion.

definition: Making someone believe that an idea is true or reasonable.
example: She gave a convincing reason for changing the timetable.

definition: Standards used to judge or choose something.
example: We agreed on three criteria for choosing a book.

definition: To recognise or show the difference between things.
example: Can you distinguish a fact from an opinion?

definition: To give particular attention or importance to something.
example: I want to emphasise the value of regular practice.

definition: To judge the quality or value of something.
example: We evaluate our project after each lesson.

definition: Information that supports a belief or conclusion.
example: The writer uses evidence to support the argument.

definition: To put a plan or decision into action.
example: We will implement the new timetable next week.

definition: To explain or understand the meaning of something.
example: Readers may interpret the ending in different ways.

definition: To discuss something in order to reach an agreement.
example: The students negotiate the division of work.

definition: Something treated as more important than other things.
example: Making the instructions clear is our first priority.

definition: Good at finding ways to solve a problem.
example: Our resourceful group made a game from old cards.

definition: Able to continue without exhausting resources.
example: Cycling is a sustainable way to travel short distances.

definition: To make a problem or discomfort less severe.
example: A short break can alleviate stress.

definition: Clear and organised so its parts fit together.
example: The essay presents a coherent argument.

definition: Strong enough to attract attention or persuade.
example: She offered a compelling reason to protect the park.

definition: To think carefully about an idea or possibility.
example: Take a moment to contemplate the question.

definition: A difference between things that should agree.
example: We found a discrepancy between the two reports.

definition: To give more information about an idea.
example: Could you elaborate on your suggestion?

definition: Possible and practical to do.
example: A weekly reading club is feasible with our current timetable.

definition: Existing as a natural or essential part of something.
example: Every new project has inherent uncertainty.

definition: Paying very close attention to details.
example: The editor made a meticulous check of every page.

definition: A small difference in meaning, feeling, or expression.
example: A change in tone adds a new nuance to the sentence.

definition: Seeming reasonable or likely to be true.
example: That is a plausible explanation for the delay.

definition: Dealing with things in a practical way.
example: We chose a pragmatic solution that used existing materials.

definition: Very deep or having a strong effect.
example: The conversation had a profound effect on her outlook.

definition: To find a way for different ideas or needs to fit together.
example: We need to reconcile the two groups' expectations.

definition: Careful and detailed examination.
example: The proposal received close scrutiny from the group.

definition: Not obvious and requiring care to notice.
example: There is a subtle difference between the two phrases.

definition: Not yet definite or certain.
example: We made a tentative plan for the next meeting.

definition: Open and easy to understand rather than hidden.
example: A transparent process helps everyone understand the decision.

definition: Never having happened or been known before.
example: The library received an unprecedented number of visitors.

definition: Able to be used for many purposes or do different things.
example: A notebook is a versatile tool for language study.
